title: AI-BAAM: AI-Driven Bank Statement Analytics as Alternative Data for Malaysian MSME Credit Scoring
authors: Kok Hoe Ng, Fadhlan Hafizhelmi Kamaru Zaman, Mohd Fauzi Othman, Weng Kin Lai, Muhammad Izzuddin Rumee
tldr: Proposes AI-BAAM, an AI-driven bank statement analytics pipeline using Logistic Regression with WOE/IV feature selection, template-matching OCR, and cash flow analysis to achieve AUROC 0.806 for MSME credit scoring, a 24.6% improvement over traditional application-only models.
problem_and_motivation: MSMEs globally face a credit gap of $5.2 trillion, with 68% lacking access to formal credit due to insufficient credit history. Traditional credit scoring relying on application-only data fails to capture true financial health; bank transaction data offers rich alternative indicators but remains underutilized due to complexity.
approach: CRISP-DM methodology for structuring the machine learning lifecycle.
Six-module cash flow underwriting workflow: Key Information Extraction, Transaction Table Extraction, Fraud Analysis, Network Analysis, Cash Flow Analysis, Data & Scoring.
Template-matching approach for OCR extraction of bank statement data achieving 0.01s per document, 100% accuracy, $0 cost.
Feature engineering using Weight of Evidence (WOE) and Information Value (IV) framework for variable selection.
Logistic Regression as primary classifier for interpretable credit scoring.
Dataset of 611 loan applicants from a Malaysian consulting firm with bank statements and application data.
Comparison of application-only features vs. bank statement features vs. combined features for model performance.
Three simulated scenarios: single-borrower, joint-borrower with weaker co-borrower, joint-borrower with stronger co-borrower.
findings: num: Logistic Regression with bank statement features achieved AUROC 0.806, a 24.6% improvement over application-only models (AUROC 0.647).
num: Combined application + bank statement features achieved AUROC 0.832, a 28.6% improvement over application-only.
num: Model with only bank statement features outperformed application-only models, demonstrating value of transaction data for thin-file borrowers.
num: Template matching for OCR extraction achieved 100% accuracy at 0.01 seconds per document with zero cost.
cat: Fraud analysis module generated a 'Red Flag' metric by flagging inconsistent information between application data and bank statements.
cat: Cash flow analysis provided holistic understanding of income and expenditure patterns over 6-12 month windows.
cat: Network analysis identified financial interconnectedness and potential business linkages among applicants.
cat: Simulated scenarios showed single-borrower model already improved; joint-borrower with stronger co-borrower yielded best risk assessment.

key_equations.equation: WOE = ln(% of Non-events / % of Events) × 100 per bin
key_equations.explanation: Weight of Evidence measures the strength of each feature bin in separating good (non-event) from bad (event) borrowers.
Information Value quantifies the overall predictive power of a feature. IV > 0.30 indicates a strong predictor.

definitions.definition: A measure of how well a feature distinguishes between good and bad credit risks, calculated as the log-ratio of non-event to event proportions per bin.
A metric that aggregates WOE across all bins of a feature to quantify its overall predictive strength in credit scoring.
A credit assessment approach that evaluates loan applicants based on their actual bank transaction history rather than self-reported application data alone.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Demonstrates that bank statement alternative data alone (AUROC 0.806) substantially outperforms traditional application-only models (AUROC 0.647) for MSME credit scoring, and introduces an affordable ($0) template-matching OCR pipeline for bank statement extraction.
directly_justifies: Odin's use of bank transaction data as alternative data for credit scoring.
WOE/IV feature selection methodology for credit risk modeling.
Cash flow underwriting approach for SME lending assessment.
Interpretable Logistic Regression for regulated financial environments.
limits: Dataset limited to 611 Malaysian loan applicants from a single consulting firm.
Template-matching OCR only works with standardized Malaysian bank statement formats.
Logistic Regression may not capture complex non-linear patterns; no comparison with XGBoost or deep learning.
Model not validated on out-of-time or out-of-sample data from different economic periods.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Algorithmic credit scoring paper using ML with bank statement alternative data. Covers credit risk, lending, cash flow analysis, ML modeling, and quantitative methodology.

limitations: Small dataset of 611 loan applicants from a single source limits generalizability.
Template-matching OCR approach is format-dependent and may not generalize to other bank statement layouts.
Logistic Regression, while interpretable, may underperform compared to ensemble or deep learning methods on complex patterns.
No external validation on out-of-time or cross-institutional datasets.
Potential sample bias: labeled default data from a single consulting firm's portfolio.
remember_this: Bank statement features alone (AUROC 0.806) beat application-only models (AUROC 0.647) by 24.6%.
WOE/IV framework for transparent, interpretable feature selection in credit scoring.
